fields.label: Key-holder plugin
fields.help: Installed on the Firebird server; supplies the key material needed to read the backup and encrypt the restored database.

fields.label: Encryption key name
fields.help: Selects the restored database's key; leave empty to inherit the backup header's key name. The key holder must supply both the backup key and any new destination key. Native gbak inserts this name into an SQL KEY clause without quoting. Restore errors can leave a partial destination database.

fields.label: Restored database encryption plugin
fields.help: Leave empty to inherit the backup header's plugin. An override selects the restored database's plugin, not the plugin used to read the backup. Both plugins must be installed on the Firebird server.

fields.label: Physical backup filename on the Firebird server
fields.help: Physical backup requires a writable database. Use logical backup for a read-only database.

fields.label: Incremental backup level
fields.help: 0 creates a full backup. A positive level requires the preceding level in backup history. Restore the complete chain in order.

fields.label: Database backup GUID (overrides level)
fields.help: Enter a hyphenated UUID, with or without braces. The native request always uses braces so it cannot be mistaken for a backup level.

fields.label: Backup read I/O policy
fields.help: Default: ON on Windows servers, OFF elsewhere. Direct reads require filesystem support.

fields.label: Clean backup history after backup
fields.help: Removes native backup-history records, not backup files. Older level/GUID lookup may no longer be possible; keep an independently verified restore chain.

fields.label: Keep backup history by
fields.help: Pruning can remove level/GUID lookup records. Backup files are kept.

fields.label: Ordered backup files
fields.help: New restore: full backup, then increments in order. In-place: increments only.
